business_problem: Adopting cloud database technology As it began transitioning to a microservices-based architecture, Victoria’s Secret initially adopted CouchDB because it was immediately compatible with the company’s virtual private cloud (VPC) operating system.
solution_summary: Adopting cloud database technology As it began transitioning to a microservices-based architecture, Victoria’s Secret initially adopted CouchDB because it was immediately compatible with the company’s virtual private cloud (VPC) operating system. After adopting microservices, the company transformed its database architecture using MongoDB Atlas. But during the standard lift-and-shift migration to Azure — which involves moving applications to the cloud without significant changes — the company carried over the existing deployment setup along with all its overhead and costs. This accelerated the migration but left the retailer with several limitations and most of its previous challenges. The CouchDB database lacked clustering and clustered indexing, which led to frequent data duplication, higher costs, and limited availability.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
solution_components.role: Retrieves semantically relevant context from Victoria's Secret's data for AI, search, and recommendation workflows.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Online Archive
solution_components.role: Moves colder data out of the hot cluster while keeping it available for retention, analysis, and compliance.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Data Federation
solution_components.role: Lets Victoria's Secret query operational and archived data together from one interface.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the managed document database backing Victoria's Secret's modernized application platform.

data_flow: Business documents, tickets, records, and other operational content stay in MongoDB Atlas Vector Search and MongoDB Atlas Online Archive, where search indexes or vector embeddings are built and then queried in real time to supply grounded results to applications, assistants, or discovery features. Upstream and downstream integrations include AWS, Azure, APIs.
business_outcome: 90% reduction in number of disks provisioned 80% reduction in disk hydration time for caching 240% improvement in API performance 75% fewer CPU cores used
metrics: It migrated more than 4 TB of data across 200 databases with zero downtime, improving scalability and cost.
architecture_clues: The solution uses a microservices-based architecture.
Vector search is part of the retrieval layer for semantic or generative-AI use cases.
Cold data retention is handled with archiving to control active storage costs.
